bundles.name: Identity and designation
bundles.description: Everything needed to say which organization is being referred to: its names across time, language and script; its identifiers under external schemes; the canonical key the adopting Dimension uses; and the evidence needed to resolve or reject a candidate match.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG models identifier and naming as first-class but under-specified properties; LEI-CDF, the ISO 6523 ICD register and BODS all show that a usable organization identity is a scheme-qualified pair plus temporal name history, not a single string. Duplicate resolution is a distinct concern because LEI registration explicitly carries a DUPLICATE status, proving that identity collisions occur in governed registries.

layers.name: Naming and designations
layers.description: Legal, trading, former, abbreviated and transliterated names of the organization, each with language, script, kind and validity in time.

findings.name: Name forms, kinds and validity periods
findings.description: An organization carries several simultaneous name forms with different legal weight. LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalName from OtherEntityNames, schema.org separates legalName from name and alternateName, and BODS separates name from alternateNames. Each form needs a kind, a language tag, and an explicit validity interval because names change without changing identity.

findings.name: Name history and change tracking
findings.description: Former names must remain retrievable and ordered, because lookups, sanctions screening and lineage tracing rely on historical strings. Companies House exposes previous_company_names as a first-class array and LEI-CDF carries name changes inside LegalEntityEvents; a purely current-state name model loses answerable history.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Name history is derived from lifecycle event records and name evidence records already held elsewhere in this model; it is an ordered projection over those artifacts, so materialising a separate artifact would duplicate evidence and create a second place for the same facts to drift.

layers.name: Identifier schemes and canonical keys
layers.description: Externally issued, scheme-qualified identifiers for the organization, and the internal canonical key used when no authoritative identifier exists.

findings.name: Scheme-qualified external identifiers
findings.description: An organization identifier is meaningless without its scheme. ISO 6523 ICD codes pair a numeric scheme designator with a value (0199 for LEI, 0060 for D-U-N-S, 0208 for the Belgian enterprise number); LEI-CDF pairs RegistrationAuthorityID with RegistrationAuthorityEntityID; BODS requires id plus scheme/schemeName or uri; and the EU EUID must itself be ISO 6523 compliant.

findings.name: Canonical key selection and internal identity
findings.description: Because many organizations hold several external identifiers and many hold none, the model must state a deterministic priority for choosing the canonical key: authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Dates, names and addresses are never keys.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The canonical key and its priority tier are pure record metadata carried inline on the organization record; there is no external document to retain, and materialising a key artifact would create an independently mutable copy of the very value that must be immutable.

findings.name: Entity resolution, matching evidence and duplicates
findings.description: Governed registries themselves record duplicates — LEI RegistrationStatus includes DUPLICATE, and Companies House exposes partial_data_available and etag for concurrency. A defensible model therefore records the evidence, method and confidence behind every merge or split rather than asserting a silent match.

bundles.name: Classification, legal form and declared purpose
bundles.description: How the organization is typed by governed code lists (legal form, entity category, activity, statistical unit) and what it declares about its own purpose, non-profit character and scale.
bundles.rationale: Legal form (ISO 20275), activity (NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 5) and entity category (LEI-CDF) are all governed, versioned, jurisdiction-bound code lists whose assignments carry their own validity and evidence. Eurostat's register manual shows that statistical unit type is a separate classification that must not be confused with identity. Purpose and scale are self-declared and therefore need a different evidence treatment from coded classifications.

layers.name: Legal form and entity category
layers.description: The organization's legal form under its jurisdiction of formation, its entity category and subcategory, and whether it has separate legal personality at all.

findings.name: Entity legal form assignment
findings.description: Legal form is a four-character ELF code valid only in combination with a jurisdiction, drawn from a list of more than 3,600 forms across more than 200 jurisdictions. The reserved codes 8888 (form not yet listed) and 9999 (no separate legal form) make the absence of a form explicitly representable rather than null.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The legal form assignment is a coded reference into an externally governed list; the authoritative artifact is the ELF code list itself, which is maintained upstream and referenced by version rather than copied, and the evidencing constitutive document is already held by the formation-act finding.

findings.name: Entity category, subcategory and legal personality
findings.description: LEI-CDF categorises entities as BRANCH, GENERAL, FUND, SOLE_PROPRIETOR, RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY or INTERNATIONAL_ORGANIZATION, with government subcategories. Category determines which other findings are even applicable and whether the subject has separate legal personality — a branch and a sole proprietorship do not.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Category and personality are coded assertions evaluated against the constitutive act and register record; both evidencing artifacts already exist in the formation and registry-entry findings, and duplicating them here would split the evidence chain.

findings.name: Organization formality spectrum
findings.description: org:Organization is a collection of people with a common purpose that can act as an agent, including informal communities. org:FormalOrganization is recognized in the world at large, especially in legal jurisdictions, with rights and responsibilities (corporation, charity, government, church). rov:RegisteredOrganization / CBV Legal Entity is a formal organization that gained legal status through a registration process and excludes natural persons, virtual organizations and agents that can act without that registration. Many organizations are not legal entities; some umbrellas contain several legal entities. Unregistered collectives remain in scope of this model as Organization, not as RegisteredOrganization.

findings.name: National legal form vocabulary
findings.description: Each jurisdiction maintains a limited set of recognized company or entity types (Plc, GmbH, SA, LLP and so on). Lexically identical labels can have different legal meanings across borders. RegOrg orgType and CBV legal form type are SKOS/code list specializations of org:classification. ELF is the cross-border alignment, not a replacement for the national register's form code when that register is the master system.

layers.name: Activity and statistical classification
layers.description: Coded economic-activity assignments under versioned schemes, and the organization's relationship to statistical units used by official registers.

findings.name: Activity code assignments across schemes
findings.description: Activity classification is scheme-bound and revision-bound: NACE Rev. 2.1 applies to European statistics from 2025 under Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/137, ISIC Rev. 5 was endorsed in 2023, and national registers use their own lists such as UK SIC. An assignment without its scheme version is not interpretable.

findings.name: Statistical unit alignment
findings.description: Official registers hold enterprise group, enterprise and local unit as mandatory statistical units alongside legal units and their links, because an enterprise may span several legal units and group boundaries follow control rather than legal personality. Recording this alignment prevents an agent from silently merging legal units into one organization or splitting an organization to match a statistical unit.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Statistical unit alignment is an assertion linking this record to units held in an external statistical register; the authoritative artifact is that register's own record, which is not redistributable in most jurisdictions, so only the reference and its provenance are retained.

layers.name: Declared purpose and scale
layers.description: What the organization states about its own mission, non-profit character and size, and how those self-declarations are dated and evidenced.

findings.name: Declared purpose, object clause and non-profit status
findings.description: W3C ORG models purpose as a first-class property and schema.org exposes nonprofitStatus and ownershipFundingInfo. Purpose statements are either constitutive (an object clause in the charter) or self-declared marketing text, and the two carry very different weight; non-profit status is a jurisdiction-granted determination, not a self-description.

findings.name: Scale, workforce and size-class measures
findings.description: Size indicators such as headcount are measurements with a method, unit, reference period and source, not static attributes. schema.org exposes numberOfEmployees and statistical registers hold size variables; without a reference period and a counting basis (headcount, full-time equivalent, including or excluding contractors) the figure is not comparable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Size measures are reported values whose evidencing documents (annual accounts, statistical returns) belong to reporting and financial models outside this scope; retaining a separate artifact here would duplicate filings already covered by the recurring-obligations finding.

bundles.name: Formation, registration standing and lifecycle
bundles.description: How the organization came into existence, where it is recorded, what its current standing is, what recurring obligations keep that standing alive, and how it changes or ends.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF separates EntityStatus from RegistrationStatus, proving that the subject's existence and the record's standing are independent state machines; Companies House adds a twelve-value national status enumeration plus status detail; W3C ORG models ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultedFrom for succession; and the EU BRIS regime requires a register-issued identifier for companies and branches. These are distinct, separately answerable concerns.

layers.name: Formation and registry entries
layers.description: The constitutive act that created the organization and the entries that public and private registers hold about it.

findings.name: Formation act and creation date
findings.description: LEI-CDF records EntityCreationDate as the legal establishment date, schema.org records foundingDate and foundingLocation, BODS records foundingDate and formedByStatute, and Companies House records date_of_creation. Formation date and first registration date are frequently different and must not be conflated.

findings.name: Registry entry and registration authority
findings.description: An entry links the organization to an authoritative source through a register code plus a local entity number, as in LEI-CDF's RegistrationAuthorityID and RegistrationAuthorityEntityID, drawing on a governed list of more than 1,050 registers across 232 jurisdictions. The EU adds the EUID, which must be ISO 6523 compliant and unequivocally identify companies and branches across interconnected registers.

findings.name: Home legal jurisdiction
findings.description: LEI-CDF LegalJurisdiction is the jurisdiction of legal formation and registration and is the jurisdiction on which LegalForm depends. It is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code or an ISO 3166-2 region code, uppercase. French overseas territories sharing French legal forms are treated as France for legal jurisdiction in the ELF list implementation. Home jurisdiction is not necessarily the headquarters country or the tax residence.

layers.name: Standing, status and recurring obligations
layers.description: The organization's current legal standing, the separate standing of each record about it, and the periodic acts required to keep both current.

findings.name: Entity status distinguished from record registration status
findings.description: LEI-CDF keeps EntityStatus (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, NULL — whether the entity is legally registered and operating) strictly separate from RegistrationStatus (PENDING_VALIDATION, ISSUED, DUPLICATE, LAPSED, RETIRED, ANNULLED, CANCELLED, TRANSFERRED, PENDING_TRANSFER, PENDING_ARCHIVAL — the standing of the record). Companies House adds a twelve-value national enumeration plus company_status_detail. Collapsing these into one status field destroys answerability.

findings.name: Recurring filing and renewal obligations
findings.description: Standing is maintained by periodic acts: LEI records carry NextRenewalDate and lapse if not renewed, and national registers require confirmation statements and accounts with their own due dates. Missing a due date changes record standing without changing the organization's existence.

layers.name: Lifecycle events and succession
layers.description: Discrete events that change the organization or its record, and the lineage links that connect predecessor and successor organizations.

findings.name: Lifecycle event records
findings.description: LEI-CDF v3.1 introduced LegalEntityEvents as a container carrying event type, dates, validation documents and the fields affected. W3C ORG models ChangeEvent linked by changedBy and resultedFrom. An event record must separate the date the event legally took effect from the date it was recorded and the date it was observed.

findings.name: Succession, continuity and lineage
findings.description: W3C ORG treats an organization resulting from a change event as sufficiently distinct to have its own identity, linked to originalOrganization; LEI-CDF carries SuccessorEntity with SuccessorLEI or SuccessorEntityName; Eurostat register practice defines continuity rules for unit births and deaths. The hard question is when a change preserves identity and when it creates a new subject.

findings.name: Dissolution and expiry
findings.description: An organization ceases as a subject by dissolution, completion of winding-up, or replacement through corporate action. schema.org dissolutionDate is a secondary discovery field. LEI RETIRED means the entity ceased without merger; INACTIVE covers closure, acquisition or illegitimacy. Identifier records are not reused. History remains queryable after cessation. Deletion of the subject record is a retention decision, not an automatic consequence of dissolution.

bundles.name: Control, ownership and representation
bundles.description: External relationships that determine who controls the organization, who owns or benefits from it, and who may act for it.
bundles.rationale: RR-CDF defines a normative, period-bounded and quantified model of consolidation and fund relationships with explicit reporting exceptions; BODS defines a statement-based model of ownership and control interests with direct/indirect and share ranges; ISO 5009 supplies codes for official roles tied to legal forms and explicitly excludes internal functional titles. Together they establish that control, ownership and representation are three distinct relationship families with different evidence regimes.

layers.name: Group structure and ownership
layers.description: Consolidation and group membership links, and ownership or control interests including beneficial ownership.

findings.name: Consolidation, branch and fund relationship links
findings.description: RR-CDF records IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF, IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY, IS_SUBFUND_OF and IS_FEEDER_TO, each with up to three distinct period types, a status, quantifiers with a measurement method, and eight exception reasons for when a parent cannot be reported.

findings.name: Ownership and beneficial-ownership interests
findings.description: BODS models ownership and control as relationship records with a subject entity, an interested party, and an array of interests each carrying type, directOrIndirect, a beneficialOwnershipOrControl flag valid only for natural persons, share values expressible as exact figures or as minimum/maximum ranges, and start and end dates. Indirect chains are represented through component records rather than collapsed edges.

layers.name: Official roles, representation and affiliation
layers.description: Who is empowered to act for the organization under law, and which external bodies the organization is affiliated with or accredited by.

findings.name: Official organizational roles and authorised representation
findings.description: ISO 5009 codes cover over 2,000 official roles across almost 250 legal forms in 89 jurisdictions, are tied to the relevant ELF code, include only roles appearing in local legislation, and explicitly exclude internal functional titles such as Chief Risk Officer. W3C ORG separates Role, Post and Membership. This finding covers the organization-side view: which posts exist and what they authorise, not the persons filling them.

findings.name: External affiliation, membership and accreditation
findings.description: Organizations belong to federations, chambers, standards bodies and networks, and hold accreditations or certifications granted by external bodies. W3C ORG models Membership as an n-ary relation between agent, organization and role; schema.org exposes memberOf and hasCredential. These links are neither ownership nor control and must not be conflated with them.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Affiliation and accreditation evidence is issued and published by the conferring body, which is a separate organization subject; this model retains only the scheme-qualified link, validity and verification endpoint, because copying certificates would create an unmaintained duplicate of another party's authoritative record.

bundles.name: Presence and reachability
bundles.description: Where the organization is legally seated, where it actually operates, and through which electronic addresses and channels it can be reached.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalAddress from HeadquartersAddress and OtherAddresses with transliterated variants; W3C ORG separates hasRegisteredSite from hasSite; Companies House exposes registered_office_is_in_dispute and undeliverable_registered_office_address, proving that a registered address is a legal construct that can be contested or non-functional; and Peppol shows that electronic addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity.

layers.name: Locations, sites and channels
layers.description: Registered and operating locations of the organization together with its electronic addresses and public channels, each with a role, validity and reachability status.

findings.name: Registered office and legal address
findings.description: The registered office is the address at which the organization is legally addressable in its jurisdiction of formation; it is frequently not an operating location and may be a service-provider address. National registers record when it is in dispute or undeliverable, which are distinct states from being absent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Registered address values are carried inline on the organization record and evidenced by the registry extract artifact already retained by the registry-entry finding; geometry, building identity and postal normalisation belong to the referenced place model rather than to a duplicated artifact here.

findings.name: Operating sites, branches and service areas
findings.description: W3C ORG models Site as a place where an organization operates and separates hasSite from hasRegisteredSite. Operating presence is distinct from legal seat: a branch may be separately registered and separately identified, while a site may be purely operational with no registry footprint at all.

findings.name: Electronic addresses and public channels
findings.description: Electronic business addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity: a Peppol participant is addressed as an ISO 6523 scheme designator plus a value, for example 0199 with an LEI or 0208 with a Belgian enterprise number. Public channels such as websites and published contact points are separate, weaker assertions that require their own verification.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Electronic addresses are scheme-qualified inline values whose authoritative artifact is the network's own participant registry, queried by resolution rather than copied; retaining a local artifact would produce stale routing data with no way to detect divergence.

bundles.name: Record governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Governance of the organization record itself: where each assertion came from, how well corroborated it is, who may see it, how long it is kept, and how it maps onto external standards.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF records ValidationSources with graded corroboration levels and a ValidationAuthority, PROV-O supplies the normative vocabulary for attributing assertions to agents and deriving records from sources, BODS requires per-statement source and publication metadata including licence, and national registers expose concurrency and completeness markers. Standard alignment must be recorded as mapping with declared loss, not as conformance.

layers.name: Provenance, quality, access and retention
layers.description: Per-assertion provenance and corroboration, data-quality assessment, disclosure classification and retention rules for the organization record.

findings.name: Assertion provenance and attribution
findings.description: Every field value is an assertion by some agent from some source at some time. PROV-O supplies wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy and actedOnBehalfOf with prov:Organization as an agent type; BODS requires source type, url, retrievedAt and assertedBy on each statement. Event time and observation time must be recorded separately.

findings.name: Validation, corroboration level and data quality
findings.description: LEI-CDF grades a record's corroboration as PENDING, ENTITY_SUPPLIED_ONLY, PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED or FULLY_CORROBORATED against a named ValidationAuthority, and RR-CDF carries validation sources, documents and references. Companies House marks partial_data_available and exposes an entity tag for concurrency. Quality is therefore a declared, evidenced grade rather than an assumed property.

findings.name: Disclosure classification, access and retention
findings.description: Organization records mix data that registers publish freely, data that is licensed, and data that identifies natural persons and therefore carries privacy obligations. BODS requires an explicit licence on publication; national registers operate protected-address and secure-officer regimes; and retention must be decided per class rather than for the record as a whole.

findings.name: Record stewards
findings.description: The organization itself, acting through officers, is the steward of its own subject record. Registers hold registrar-stewarded copies. GLEIF ManagingLOU administers the LEI record. CBV legal representatives (via schema.org and related discovery) are not the same as employment posts. This layer records stewardship of data, not corporate governance of people.

layers.name: Interoperability and mapping
layers.description: Declared alignments to external standards and the recorded divergences between sources that assert different values for the same organization.

findings.name: Standard alignment, crosswalks and register divergence
findings.description: External standards are alignments, not conformance claims. W3C ORG, schema.org, LEI-CDF, NACE and ISIC each cover overlapping but non-identical ground, and national registers legitimately disagree with global ones about name, status and address. Divergence must be recorded as an observation with sources, not silently resolved.

model.name: Inter-organizational Relationship
model.purpose: Describe attributed, time-qualified organizational relationships without confusing affiliation, supply, consolidation and ownership.
model.scope_statement: A source-qualified relationship aggregate with explicit participants, kind, direction, scope and evidence. Real-world relation state, publisher record state and observer claims remain separate. Multi-party arrangements require retained membership context.
in_scope: Relationship identity, endpoint roles and qualified kind
Control-basis references, collaboration and exchange scope
Temporal assertions, graph constraints, disputes and permitted mappings
out_of_scope: Organization identity, contract execution and ownership-register mastership
Customer/account and supplier-qualification lifecycles
Inferring legal authority, beneficial ownership or universal transitivity from a generic link

boundary_notes.distinction: Reference organization identities; a relationship is not either organization.
Customer/account and supplier/partner qualification remain separate lifecycle masters; relationships provide scoped links.
Qualified relation kinds are not universally equivalent; person beneficial owners are out of endpoint scope.
PROV Association qualifies activity-agent provenance, not inter-organizational partnership; contract execution stays delegated.

functions.name: Resolve qualified relationship
functions.description: Compare identities and scopes without merging parallel relations.
preconditions: Read permission and kind definition
effects: Read-only; identity ambiguity returns candidates, never automatic same-as

functions.name: Inspect qualified graph
functions.description: Traverse asserted or explicitly derived relationships at a declared time.
preconditions: Authorized endpoints and reviewed kind-specific graph rules
effects: Read-only; unsupported transitivity or cycles yield warnings/rejection

functions.name: Record attributed assertion
functions.description: Append evidence-backed claim without creating a real-world agreement.
outputs: New immutable local assertion or conflict report
preconditions: Contributor delegation
Resolved master scope
Schema and graph checks
effects: Local append only; no signatures, payments or grants; failed checks leave head unchanged

functions.name: Append lifecycle revision
functions.description: Separate effective termination, correction and record retirement.
preconditions: Write authority
Expected head and retention check
effects: Append with compensating revision for mistakes; never erase provenance or terminate a contract

functions.name: Register counterclaim
functions.description: Preserve incompatible positions for authorized review.
outputs: Attributed contested set and review status
preconditions: Permitted evidence access
No automated truth ranking by recency alone

model.name: Offer / Quote
model.purpose: Represent one governed, versioned pre-contract commercial proposal so agents can understand who proposes what, to whom, for which price and terms, during which validity, with what evidence and response state, without confusing the proposal with a product master, negotiation, order, contract or legal formation decision.
model.scope_statement: Owns proposal identity, version, declared offer, quotation, estimate or informational profile; issuer and addressed-recipient roles; external product, service, right and resource references; lines, lots, bundles, options, alternatives and dependencies; quantities, units and eligibility; prices, currencies, formulas, tiers, recurring and usage terms; taxes, allowances, charges and totals; delivery, payment, quality, warranty, return, service-level, assumption, exclusion, rights and confidentiality terms; issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, expiry and knowledge times; attributable withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer and acceptance references; amendments, source, approval, quality, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Party, subject, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response-event and legal-determination masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Proposal identity, versions, profiles, parties by reference, offered subjects, lines, lots, bundles, quantities, eligibility, pricing, taxes, totals and commercial terms
Fulfilment conditions, validity, lifecycle, response references, amendments, evidence, provenance, validation, access, retention and interoperable projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Product, Service, Right, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Shipment, Performance, Response Event, Legal Decision or Records masters
Treating a quotation, estimate, acknowledgement, click, conduct or technical status as universal proof of legal offer, acceptance, formation or enforceability
Autonomous pricing approval, tax or legal determination, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen object parent may supply generic object context but grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: RFQ, negotiation, tender, order and contract

Parties, products, services, catalogues, RFQs, negotiations, tenders, contracts, orders, invoices, payments, fulfilment, response events, legal determinations and records remain external masters.

decisions.concept: Offer, quotation, estimate and informational proposal
decisions.rationale: The shared structure is useful, but declared intent, definiteness, governing rules and legal effect differ; no label alone determines an operative legal offer.
The registry parent signal has no frozen canonical relation and grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.
Party, subject, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment and fulfilment identities and lifecycles remain external.

decisions.concept: Line, lot, bundle, option and dependency semantics
decisions.rationale: Composition preserves stable line and term identities plus alternative, substitution, minimum, partial and all-or-none rules rather than flattening them into text.

List, unit, base, net, fixed, estimated, ranged, tiered, recurring, usage, tax, allowance, charge, subtotal and payable values stay distinct with currency, unit, quantity basis, formula, validity and provenance.

Sending, delivery, receipt, acknowledgement, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer, acceptance evidence and formation determinations are separately attributable; no status automatically proves legal effect.

Issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge times remain distinct and RFC 3339 timestamps require seconds and offset.
CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements provide scoped reference profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy and records rules remain jurisdiction-qualified.
UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI expose different subsets and never replace canonical proposal semantics.

One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts; assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-021 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-OBJ-003 is only a parent signal and no model relation is canonically approved for this aggregate.

Boundary hold: offer or quote, party, product, service, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response event, legal determination and records must retain separate identities.

Legal-effect hold: offer, quotation, estimate and informational profiles require explicit intent, governing rules and jurisdiction; no label, click, acknowledgement, conduct or status universally proves acceptance, formation or enforceability.

Pricing hold: every amount requires type, currency, unit or quantity basis, inclusion and exclusion, tax and charge treatment, formula or source, validity, rounding, approval and uncertainty qualifiers.

Temporal hold: issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge time must never be silently collapsed; timestamps require seconds and timezone offset.
Authority hold: pricing approval, tax determination, legal classification, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening and disposition require delegated accountable authority.
Jurisdiction hold: CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements are scoped profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy, records and sector rules require separate validation.
Interoperability hold: every UBL, schema.org, GS1, UNECE, ISO 4217, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI projection requires version pins, conformance evidence and information-loss declarations.

Privacy hold: recipient-specific prices, discounts, cost, margin, tax, negotiation, approval, contact, response and commercially sensitive data require purpose-bound access, minimization and retention controls.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Canonically approve the WM-OBJ-003 relation and register Party, Product, Service, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Fulfilment, Event and Records edges.
Create public procurement, securities, insurance, healthcare, utilities, travel, telecom, software subscription, construction and jurisdiction-specific profiles.
Conformance-test lines, dependencies, quantities, units, prices, taxes, totals, validity, amendments and projections against concrete UBL and commerce examples.
Validate organization-specific pricing, discount, tax, approval, signing, dispatch, publication, access, retention and disposition policies.
Obtain authorized legal and tax review before making jurisdiction-specific formation, enforceability, disclosure or tax claims.
Obtain independent external research review before promoting beyond reviewable-draft assurance.

model.name: Subscription
model.purpose: Represent one governed recurring commercial relationship so agents can understand who subscribes to which plan, which items and entitlements recur, how billing and renewal operate, what usage and service evidence exists and how cancellation progresses without confusing the subscription with its contract, invoices, payments or service instances.
model.scope_statement: Owns subscription identity, versions, profile and lifecycle; provider, subscriber, payer, beneficiary and administrator references; external contract, account, order, catalogue, offering, service and entitlement bindings; plan versions, items, add-ons, bundles, seats, assignments and dependencies; permissions, limits, usage allowances, rollover and overage references; recurring, one-time, seat, usage and tiered price rules; currencies, taxes, discounts, credits, proration and refunds; billing anchors, recurrence, periods, invoice and payment references; trial, activation, service, pause, suspension, grace and reactivation observations; term, renewal, notice, consent, cancellation and termination assertions; usage, quality, support, provenance, validation, privacy, retention and loss-aware projections. External agreement, party, product, entitlement, order, invoice, payment, usage, service, support and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Subscription identity, versions, profiles, participants, plan bindings, items, seats, beneficiaries, entitlements, usage allowances and constraints
Recurring economics, billing and renewal schedules, invoice and payment references, service and usage evidence, lifecycle, notices, cancellation, validation, access, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Contract, Party, Account, Product, Service Offering, Entitlement, Credential, Order, Invoice, Payment Method, Payment Transaction, Usage Event, Meter Reading, Service Instance, Support Case or Records masters
Treating active, paid, renewed or cancelled status as universal proof of legal validity, service delivery, entitlement, conformity, termination completion or data deletion
Autonomous contract formation, charging, invoicing, plan or price change, entitlement grant or revocation, renewal, cancellation, termination, disclosure or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen parent agreement establishes obligations and legal terms. The subscription is a recurring operational aggregate that references but does not replace the contract.
The plan or offering defines reusable terms, products and services have independent instances, and entitlements are separate grants. The subscription binds versions and observes state.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Invoice, payment mandate, payment and usage
boundary_notes.distinction: Billing schedules predict or request recurring economics, invoices assert amounts due, payments settle, and usage observations meter consumption; none is the subscription identity.
Activation, entitlement, provisioning and availability are separate processes or observations; active subscription status does not prove their success.

boundary_notes.neighbor: TM Forum, schema.org, ODRL, EPC, RFC, PROV, DQV and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has a distinct scope; every mapping is version-pinned and loss-declaring.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative subscription identifier, provider namespace and version head, never by subscriber, plan name, invoice, payment, start date or digest alone.
Keep subscription, contract, party, account, offering, entitlement, order, invoice, payment, usage, service, support and records independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare profile, identity, plan, party, item, entitlement, usage, pricing, billing, renewal, lifecycle, privacy and interoperability effects.
Issued versions are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, affected items, entitlements, bills, notices, compatibility, migration and approval.
Never silently change provider, subscriber, plan, item, beneficiary, price, currency, tax, recurrence, term, renewal, entitlement, cancellation, authority or privacy term.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, version, plan, parties, items, entitlements, economics, schedules, lifecycle, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins specification version and declares loss in plan, entitlement, usage, billing, renewal, cancellation, authority and temporal semantics.

artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish signup, contract, trial, activation, service, usage, billing, invoice, payment, renewal, notice, cancellation, termination, observation, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, subscription and version IDs, profile, provider, actor, recurrence and timezone, distinct event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The subscription owns recurring-relationship context but not external contract, party, product, entitlement, invoice, payment, usage, service or records masters.
Agreement, entitlement, provisioning, service, billing, payment and usage states and clocks remain distinct.
Active, paid or renewed status never alone proves legal validity, entitlement delivery, service availability, conformity or future payment.
Agents cannot autonomously form contracts, change plans or prices, charge, invoice, grant or revoke entitlements, renew, cancel, terminate, disclose or dispose records without delegated authority.

model.name: Sales Lead / Opportunity
model.purpose: Represent one governed commercial pursuit from an originating lead signal through an explicitly qualified opportunity so agents can coordinate need, fit, stakeholders, activities, value, stage, probability, forecast and outcome without confusing the pursuit with party, customer, account, campaign, offering, quote, order, contract or revenue masters.
model.scope_statement: Owns pursuit identity, version, profile and status; signal, source and attribution; need, demand, problem, outcome and use-case assertions; qualification dimensions and decisions; offering-fit, scope, quantity, location, timing and dependency assertions; estimated value, budget, amount type, currency, recurrence, range and basis; score, method, version, explanation, confidence, bias and calibration; stage, gate and exception assertions; probability, forecast category, expected-close and as-of assertions; stakeholder, owner, team, influence and decision-group roles; interaction, activity and next-action references; capture, deduplication, merge, split, qualify, convert, nurture, hold, reopen, win, loss, no-decision and closure evidence; quote, order, contract and outcome references; distinct clocks, provenance, privacy, retention, validation and loss-aware projections. External party, customer, account, campaign, product, offering, activity, communication, calendar, quote, order, contract, fulfilment, forecast, financial and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Pursuit identity, version, classification, lineage, origin, attribution, need, demand, offering fit, scope, quantity, timing, location, dependencies and estimated value

Qualification, score, stage, gates, probability, forecast, stakeholders, consent and preference bindings, activities, next actions, conversion, closure, outcome, clocks, provenance, privacy, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Contact, Organization, Customer, Account, Campaign, Product, Offering, Activity, Message, Calendar, Quote, Order, Contract, Fulfilment, Invoice, Payment, Revenue, Forecast Period, Records or Consent masters

Treating a lead signal as a known person, a known party as a qualified lead, a qualified lead as a customer, or qualification, score, stage, probability, forecast and outcome as mutually proving facts

Autonomous contact, consent creation, sensitive-attribute inference, adverse action, pricing, quote issuance, order acceptance, contract execution, forecast commitment, financial recognition, disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified registry supplies only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger has no settled edge. Customer and account relationships remain external; a pursuit binds them when known.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Lead signal, party, contact, customer and account
boundary_notes.distinction: Signals may be anonymous or inferred, parties and contacts have external identities, and customer or account status has its own authority. Conversion preserves lineage instead of collapsing these identities.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Campaign, offering, activity, message and calendar
boundary_notes.distinction: Attribution, fit and touchpoints are typed references; their content, execution, delivery, scheduling and master lifecycle stay external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Quote, order, contract, fulfilment, forecast and finance
boundary_notes.distinction: Estimated value and probability support a pursuit but are not price, quotation, commitment, order, contract, delivery, recognized revenue or cash. Those masters retain independent authority.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-ORG-014 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen candidate relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-026 edge.
Business-to-business, consumer, public-sector, partner, marketplace, tender, subscription, regulated-sector and regional pursuits need separate profiles.
Qualification frameworks, score models, calibration, probability, forecast taxonomies, fiscal periods, quotas and revenue-recognition links require organization-specific validation.
TMF699 official path and visible release labelling are inconsistent, and every TMF, UBL, Schema.org, privacy, ORG, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI mapping needs release-pinned conformance tests.
conflicts: Lead signal, known party, qualified lead, customer or account and opportunity are related but not interchangeable.
Qualification, score, stage, probability, forecast category, expected close and actual outcome belong to separate assertion axes.
Estimated value, budget, list price, quote, order, contract, recognized revenue and cash are related but not equivalent.
Purpose, lawful basis, consent, preference and channel permission may differ and must coexist with jurisdiction and objection evidence.
regional_assumptions: Marketing contact, consent, profiling, direct marketing, record retention, tendering and contracting depend on jurisdiction, channel, sector and party type.
GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive and FTC CAN-SPAM guidance are scoped profiles, not universal law, and local implementations may add obligations.
adversarial_checks: Reject a pursuit that absorbs party, customer, account, campaign, catalog, activity, message, quote, order, contract, fulfilment or finance masters.
Reject conversion that collapses a signal, party, lead, account and opportunity into one identity.
Reject qualification, score, probability or forecast without source, method, version, evidence, as-of time, confidence, calibration and contestability.
Reject value without amount type, currency, range, recurrence, basis and explicit non-equivalence to price or commitment.
Reject autonomous contact, consent creation, sensitive-attribute inference, adverse action, forecast commitment, quote, order, contract, disclosure or destruction without authority.
Reject a projection that hides stage, scoring, probability, value, privacy, authority, provenance or information loss.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a versioned commercial-pursuit aggregate spanning a lead signal to an explicitly qualified opportunity. Party, customer, account, campaign, product, offering, activity, communication, quote, order, contract, fulfilment, forecast, finance and records masters remain external.

decisions.rationale: One pursuit can bind signal, need, qualification, fit, stage, stakeholders, value, forecast and outcome evidence without absorbing adjacent identity, communication, commercial or financial masters.
The unified registry supplies a parent hint but the frozen relation ledger has no settled WM-ECO-026 edge. It grants no containment or cascade authority.

decisions.concept: Signal, party, lead, customer, account and opportunity
decisions.rationale: A signal may be anonymous, a party is not a qualified lead, and neither a lead nor opportunity proves customer or account status. Conversion records lineage.
Expressed and inferred needs remain distinguishable and contestable, while offerings and specifications remain external versioned catalogue records.

decisions.concept: Qualification, score, stage, probability and forecast
decisions.rationale: Each axis carries its own method, version, evidence, authority, confidence and as-of time. None is promoted to objective fact or allowed to prove another.
Budget and estimated value are typed estimates and never substitute for price, quote, order, contract, recognized revenue or cash.
The pursuit binds roles and external activity references. It cannot autonomously contact a person, create consent, send a message or mutate calendar and communication masters.
GDPR, ePrivacy and FTC guidance are scoped profiles. Purpose, lawful basis, consent, preference, objection and channel permission remain separate and no sensitive-attribute inference is permitted.
Lifecycle changes preserve prior identities, source evidence, reasons, authority and clocks rather than overwriting history or cascading into adjacent masters.
TM Forum, UBL, Schema.org, privacy, ORG, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI cover different facets and never replace the canonical pursuit aggregate.
The official URL path and visible release labelling are inconsistent; the mapping stays provisional until a release-specific artefact and conformance suite are pinned.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-026 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-ORG-014 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-026 edge.
Identity hold: lead signal, known party, qualified lead, customer or account and opportunity remain distinct and conversion preserves lineage.
Methodology hold: qualification dimensions, stages, scores, probabilities and forecast categories require organization-specific definitions, versioning, calibration and review.
Bias and profiling hold: score and propensity features require purpose, lawful basis, minimization, fairness, explanation, contestability and prohibited-attribute controls.
Commercial boundary hold: estimated value, budget, offer, list price, quote, order, contract, forecast, recognized revenue and cash remain distinct.
Communication hold: purpose, lawful basis, consent, preference, objection and channel permission remain separate; agents cannot autonomously contact or create consent.
Jurisdiction hold: GDPR, ePrivacy and FTC CAN-SPAM are scoped profiles; national, sector, consumer, employment, competition, tender and records rules need validation.
TMF699 source hold: the official URL path and visible release labelling are inconsistent, so the mapping requires release-specific confirmation.
State-axis hold: qualification, score, stage, probability, forecast category, expected close, actual close and outcome states and clocks must not collapse.
Authority hold: merge, conversion, stage change, contact, quote, order, contract, forecast commitment, disclosure and destruction require delegated authority.
Interoperability hold: every TMF, UBL, Schema.org, privacy, ORG, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI projection needs release pins, conformance evidence and loss declarations.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Marketing Campaign
model.purpose: Represent one governed marketing campaign so agents can coordinate objectives, audiences, propositions, channels, content, schedule, budget, measurement, execution, experiments, optimization and learning without confusing campaign state with communication delivery, audience consent, sales conversion, financial commitment or causal effect.
model.scope_statement: Owns marketing-campaign identity, revisions, profiles and state; generic campaign, sponsor, owner, brand, market and initiative bindings; situation, insight, baseline, objective, intended outcome, hypothesis, target and success-criterion assertions; audience-definition, segment, taxonomy, source, recency, eligibility, exclusion, geography, language, accessibility and suppression bindings; value-proposition, product, service, offer, promotion, benefit and claim references; channel, endpoint, journey, touchpoint, activity, content, creative, message, localization and approval bindings; wave, flight, placement, inventory, partner, contract, schedule, cadence, sequence and frequency plan; planned and approved budget and resource allocations; metric definitions, numerators, denominators, units, baselines, targets, data sources, identity resolution, deduplication, attribution windows and models; execution, delivery, impression, viewability, invalid-traffic, reach, frequency, engagement, response, conversion and business-outcome references; experiment, treatment, control, assignment, contamination, effect, uncertainty and causal-limit assertions; approval, launch, pause, optimization, change, exception, incident, closure and retrospective evidence; distinct clocks, provenance, privacy, quality, retention, validation and loss-aware projections. External generic campaign, party, audience, consent, offer, promotion, advertisement, creative, activity, communication, placement, contract, finance, observation, experiment, sales and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Campaign identity, revisions, purpose, sponsor, situation, objectives, hypotheses, audiences, exclusions, propositions, channels, content, waves, placement, schedule, frequency, budget and resource allocations
Metric and attribution design, execution and performance evidence, experiments, optimization, lifecycle, outcomes, clocks, provenance, privacy, access, retention, validation and projections
out_of_scope: Owning generic Campaign, Project, Organization, Brand, Market, Product, Service, Offer, Promotion, Advertisement, Creative Work, Content, Audience Member, Segment, Party, Contact Point, Consent, Preference, Activity, Event, Communication, Channel Endpoint, Placement, Inventory, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Budget Ledger, Dataset, Metric Definition, Observation, Experiment, Sales Lead, Opportunity, Customer, Account or Records masters

Treating campaign state as proof of delivery, impression, viewability, reach, engagement, response, conversion, revenue, consent or causality, or treating one funnel, attribution method, KPI, taxonomy or channel as universal

Autonomous targeting of protected groups, unlawful contact, consent creation, sensitive-attribute inference, dark patterns, discrimination, claim approval, content publication, media purchase, budget commitment, personal-data disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified registry supplies a provisional parent signal only. The generic campaign coordinates activities toward an outcome; this aggregate adds marketing-specific audience, proposition, channel, content, budget and measurement context without a settled containment edge.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ECO-028 Advertisement / Promotion, Offer, Product, Service and Creative Work
boundary_notes.distinction: The campaign binds propositions and exact external content or promotion revisions. It neither defines the promoted subject nor owns advertisement, creative, offer or promotion lifecycles.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audience, Party, Contact, Consent, Preference and Communication
boundary_notes.distinction: The campaign owns intended-audience definitions and purpose-scoped bindings, not person identity, membership truth, contact permission, suppression authority or message dispatch.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Activity, placement, event, observation, experiment and sales outcome
boundary_notes.distinction: Execution and performance are source-qualified external evidence. Campaign state does not prove delivery or outcome, attribution does not prove causality, and leads or opportunities keep their own identity.

boundary_notes.neighbor: TM Forum, IAB Tech Lab, Schema.org, privacy law, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation covers only a facet or profile; every mapping is version-pinned, jurisdiction-qualified and loss-declaring.
